2	
3	**Owner:** elio (execution) + vega (review gate)
4	**Source intel:** decoder supplement niche batch 2026-04-27 (AG1, Ritual, Hims, Care/of, Magic Spoon, Liquid IV)
5	**Status:** ACTIVE — supplement-niche-validated 2026-04-27. Expand with apparel/beauty batches as teardowns complete.
6	**Stack scope:** Stack B (Shopify Native) + Stack C (Shopify External standalone)
7	**Counterpart copy file:** `~/.claude/memory/content/ecom/objection-handling-library.md`
8	**CRO playbook:** `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/cro-decoded-patterns.md` (SUP-PAT-001 through SUP-PAT-005)
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Trust Hierarchy for Supplements
13	
14	The supplement trust hierarchy governs which trust signals deserve the most visual weight and the highest page position. The order reflects the customer's mental question sequence on first visit.
15	
16	### Hierarchy (highest to lowest conversion impact)
17	
18	1. **Third-party testing certification** — NSF Certified for Sport / Informed Sport / USP Verified / Clean Label Project
19	   - Answers: "Is it safe? Was it tested by anyone independent?"
20	   - Why it ranks #1: Supplements are unregulated relative to pharmaceuticals. The first customer question is safety, not efficacy. Third-party testing removes that block before any claim can land.
21	   - Brand evidence: AG1 (NSF Certified for Sport — above fold), Ritual (Clean Label Project — above fold), Hims (Physician-backed + Certificate of Analysis)
22	
23	2. **MD / RD endorsement** — Named physician or registered dietitian with credentials visible
24	   - Answers: "Do experts actually use or endorse this?"
25	   - Why it ranks #2: Authority endorsement converts safety-concern into professional approval. Works especially well when the supplement is adjacent to a medical category (hormones, weight loss, cognition, prenatal).
26	   - Brand evidence: Ritual (named CSO + SVP Science with headshots), AG1 (Dr. Andrew Huberman endorsement), Hims (licensed physicians)
27	
28	3. **Customer review volume + qualifier** — Exact number + "verified" qualifier
29	   - Answers: "Do real people think it works?"
30	   - Why it ranks #3: After safety is addressed, social proof confirms efficacy through peer experience. Exact count ("50,000+") with "verified" qualifier outperforms star rating alone.
31	   - Brand evidence: AG1 ("50,000+ verified 5-star reviews"), Magic Spoon ("80,000+ 5-Star Reviews"), Liquid IV (testimonials in hero zone)
32	
33	4. **Press / media logos** — Named publications, not generic "as seen in"
34	   - Answers: "Has this been covered by credible third parties?"
35	   - Why it ranks #4: Press logos add mainstream legitimacy. Most effective when the publication name is recognizable to the ICP (Forbes, TIME, Vogue, Men's Health — depends on audience).
36	   - Brand evidence: AG1 (Forbes, Vogue, Bon Appétit), Magic Spoon (Forbes "future of cereal," TIME Top 100 Inventions, CNN), Liquid IV (secondary placement)
37	
38	5. **Celebrity / athlete endorsement** — Named person, not anonymous quote
39	   - Answers: "Do aspirational people I look up to use this?"
40	   - Why it ranks #5: Identity projection drives conversion when ICP buys into a performance lifestyle. Lower in hierarchy than safety cert because celebrity alone doesn't answer "is it safe."
41	   - Brand evidence: AG1 (Hugh Jackman, Allyson Felix, Lewis Hamilton), Ritual (no celebrity — intentionally avoided for scientific credibility)
42	
43	6. **Guarantee / risk reversal** — Specific outcome + specific window + self-serve refund
44	   - Answers: "What happens if it doesn't work for me?"
45	   - Why it ranks #6: Guarantee is a conversion floor, not a conversion ceiling. It closes wavering buyers but rarely creates new intent. Always present but not the top-of-funnel driver.
46	   - Brand evidence: AG1 ("90-Day Money Back Guarantee"), Magic Spoon ("Happiness 100% Guaranteed"), Liquid IV (implied returns)
47	
48	### When to reorder
49	
50	- **Mass-market / CPG ICP (e.g., Liquid IV, Magic Spoon):** Elevate review volume (#3) to #1, push safety cert down. Mass buyers trust their peers more than certifications.
51	- **Men's health / medical-adjacent ICP (e.g., Hims):** Elevate MD endorsement (#2) to #1. The physician authority resolves safety and drug-interaction concerns simultaneously.
52	- **Quiz-funnel path (e.g., Care/of):** Personalization proof replaces the entire trust hierarchy for above-fold. Below fold, restore standard order.

10	## Funnel Stages + Benchmarks
11	
12	| Stage | Median DTC | Top quartile | Boldteq target |
13	|-------|-----------|--------------|----------------|
14	| Visitor → Cart | 5-8% | 12%+ | ≥10% |
15	| Cart → Checkout | 40-50% | 65%+ | ≥55% |
16	| Checkout → Purchase | 65-75% | 85%+ | ≥80% |
17	| First Purchase → Repeat | 25-35% | 50%+ | ≥40% |
18	| Subscriber retention (90d) | 55-65% | 80%+ | ≥70% |
19

21	
22	## Lift Mandate
23	
24	40%+ relative improvement on baseline per surface tested. Baseline measured against:
25	1. Decoder bank median for same niche (until live A/B traffic available)
26	2. Live control variant (post-traffic threshold)

30	## Surface Priority Order (default)
31	
32	1. **PDP hero** — highest visitor-touch leverage (decoder confidence: high)
33	2. **Cart drawer mechanics** — every cart-creator sees
34	3. **Checkout flow** — express-first, address autocomplete, field optimization
35	4. **Post-purchase upsell** — one-click 30-min window
36	5. **Subscription toggle** — default-state per niche
37	6. **Email signup discount** — 10-15% standard
38	7. **Listing filters** — faceted UX
39	8. **FAQ structure** — objection-handling

5	
6	**Source:** ELI-011 · changelog: `~/.claude/memory/training/cycle-ecom-v1-session-3-changelog.md`
7	
8	### Confirmation Page Zone Order (ELI-011)
9	**Mandatory zone hierarchy:**
10	1. **Order details** (FIRST) — order number, ETA, items list. Reduces 'did it work?' anxiety.
11	2. **Upsell module** (SECOND) — uses 30-min one-click eligibility window (CAT-006 + ecom-cro mechanics).
12	3. **Account creation prompt + referral CTA** (THIRD) — lower-priority retention asks.
13	
14	**Anti-patterns:**
15	- Upsell first (feels pushy + hides order info, increases support tickets)
16	- Account creation first (high-friction first ask, increases bounce)
17	- Brand celebration first (feels self-indulgent before info delivered)
18	
19	**Tone:** confirmation header confident-warm ("Order confirmed!" / "You're all set, {{firstName}}.") not generic ("Thank you for your order.")
